name: text-gradient
summary: Fills the text with a gradient through background-clip: text. It takes the gradient mixin's arguments, colours first: a linear, radial or conic gradient, plain or repeating, with an optional colour space.

arguments.name: $colors
accepts: one or more colour stops, in the forms the gradient mixin takes
a stop the browser drops is refused, because the gradient and the transparent text would go with it

arguments.name: $direction
accepts: a direction name such as top or bottom-left
an angle in deg, grad, rad or turn, or 0
"to top" or "to left top" as a string

arguments.name: $shape
accepts: radial only, circle or ellipse with an optional size

arguments.name: $position
accepts: radial or conic, a position name or at followed by a position

arguments.name: $in
accepts: a colour space such as oklab, or a polar one with a hue method
the gradient is written once without the space first, for a browser that does not know it

examples: .a { @include text-gradient(red yellow lime cyan blue magenta red, conic); }
caveats: The letters have no colour of their own: the gradient is the only thing painting them. In forced colours the browser forces `background-image: none` and forces `color`, but `-webkit-text-fill-color` is not a forced property, so the transparent fill survived and the text disappeared. Since 4.0.0 a `@media (forced-colors: active)` block gives both back: measured with forced colours on, the computed fill colour was `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` before and is black now, in Chrome 152 and Firefox 156. Safari has no way to turn forced colours on from automation, so it was not measured there.
